findings.section: Behaviour contract / P2 (the Sessions block); Why this shape (schema checks)
findings.summary: The new reports no longer show which schema each session record uses, and they no longer check that it is the expected one. The Python validated every record against the version the acceptance expects: session/v3 in C5.1, session/v4 in the work, verify, gate-review, plan and second reports. The Go program validates each record against its own `schema` field. The P1 text table has no schema column, and the Sessions block names a record's schema only when the record is INVALID. A Copilot record written under the wrong version, valid against that version, would read 'schema-valid' with nothing to show the mistake. This is exactly the fact the kit's past results recorded.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/report.py: `[vloop, "schema", "validate", "session/v4", f]` in work/verify/gate-review/plan/second, `session/v3` in run; internal/driver/session.go:492-497 (Copilot plan/work/verify/gate-review and every second-review record are session/v4, the rest session/v3); tools/copilot-acceptance/README.md:121-122 ('`session/v4` validity'); docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md:248, 363, 399, 430, 474 ('every record `session/v4`'). The brief's P1 text columns: run # phase task agent model time cost source credits turns denied error (no schema).
findings.fix: Make the schema visible in the block. Either list every record as `- <folder>/sessions/<file>: <schema> ok|INVALID` (`no schema` as now), not only the rejected ones, or give the Session records line per-schema counts (`Session records: 5, schema-valid 5 (session/v3 2, session/v4 3).`). Pin the chosen form literally in P2 and in the comparison rule. If the loss is intended, say so under 'Why this shape' and in the README, so the next acceptance does not record 'every record session/v4' without having checked it.

decisions: The per-session view is a --by value of vloop metrics, not a new command. Sound: a single reader of the records.

by_session is added to metrics/v4 as an optional property, with no v5. It is emitted on every --json document, so close snapshots (.vloop/state/metrics/*.json, committed) from B37 on carry every session row, including the denial texts (masked commands and messages). export drops it. Acceptable, but the operator should know the snapshots grow.
--by session with --workspace is refused (exit 2) rather than given a repo column. Fine, and consistent with Out of scope.
The kit is one Go program under tools/copilot-acceptance/kit/, run with `go -C "$top" run`, not a vloop subcommand. This matches the tools/agent-eval precedent.

The Go program reproduces the Python byte for byte, on goldens the base's Python generates. task 2's gate regenerates them from `git show <base>:…`, so python3 stays a gate-time dependency of the repository (not of the kit or of go test).

The reports' per-kind session tables are replaced by the all-phase per-session view. Each report now lists every session, not only the phase it is about. The gate-review report loses its `round` column, and the raw permission_denials JSON becomes '- run/# phase tool: text' lines. See the finding on the lost schema version.
Where the Python's glob order is unsorted (the second report), the Go program sorts it, with the */*/ list first.
#: three digits. credits: '-' when absent, '0.00' when 0. turns falls back to num_turns for shell-loop records. These choices are sound.
The acceptance at close is the operator's: work.sh and run.sh on real Copilot with python3 shadowed, plus a check that git status --ignored is unchanged.
